> 孔德之容，惟道是從。道之為物，惟恍惟惚.

Chapter 20 ended with 貴食母 — I value feeding on the mother. Chapter 21 asks the obvious question: what is that mother like?

This is the book's most concentrated attempt to describe the Dao directly, and the passage most often read as mysticism. 恍惚, 窈冥, 有象, 有物, 有精, 有信 — six terms in a row, and it sounds like a mood.

It is actually quite concrete. Laozi is not saying what the Dao is. He is reporting what it is like when you reach for it.

## 孔德之容

The first four characters set the relation. 孔 is "great" in the old sense — the hollow, the opening; 容 is the bearing, the capacity, the container.

德's 容 — its bearing, what it can hold — is 惟道是從: it follows nothing but the Dao.

This kills a very common assumption: that 德 is a moral quality you accumulate through effort. In this line, 德 is not cultivated; it is what flows from 道, and its capacity is determined by how closely it tracks.

## 道之為物，惟恍惟惚

The Dao is described as a 物 — a thing — and then immediately as 恍惚.

恍 and 惚 are not "vague." They describe the state of an image that is present and not fixed: you see it, and the moment you try to hold the seeing, it moves.

This is the report of an instrument at its limit, the same report as chapter 14's 視之不見. The difference is that chapter 14 described the failure of the eye, ear, and hand; chapter 21 describes what is on the other side.

## 惚兮恍兮，其中有象；恍兮惚兮，其中有物

Inside the indeterminacy, there is 象 — an image, a configuration. Inside it, there is 物 — a thing.

The order matters: 象 before 物. What can be perceived first is the pattern, not the object. The object is what the pattern condenses into.

This is why the Dao can be spoken about at all: not because it is a thing you can point at, but because the pattern is legible even when the object is not.

## 窈兮冥兮，其中有精；其精甚真，其中有信

Deeper: 窈冥 — dark, profound, the depth where nothing shows.

其中有精 — inside there is 精, the essential. 其精甚真 — and that essence is real. 其中有信 — inside it there is 信.

信 here is the same word as in chapter 17: reliability, the thing that holds. So the deepest layer is not a mystery — it is the most reliable thing there is. The dark is not empty; it is where the reliable lives.

## 自今及古，其名不去，以閱眾甫

From now back to the old, its name is not lost; by it one reviews the 眾甫 — the many beginnings, all the things that have come into being.

閱 is to inspect, to review. The Dao is not the origin in a historical sense; it is the standard by which every origin can be read.

## 吾何以知眾甫之狀哉？以此

How do I know the condition of all these beginnings? By this.

以此 — by this. Not by revelation, not by tradition. By the same instrument the chapter has just described: the capacity to see the 象 before the 物, the pattern before the thing.

## What this chapter actually delivers

It does not deliver a definition. It delivers a working relation: 德 is what follows the Dao, and following it is possible because the pattern is legible even though the object is not graspable.

That is enough to build on, and it is more than a definition would give you.
